messages:
jasper: Quick sync — I sketched a "per-tenant precision sequencer" for the convo-summary model. Goal: allow phased rollouts that step tenants through FP8 -> FP8+INT8 shadow -> INT4 hotpath while keeping a strict quality guard. Thoughts? :eyes:

maria: Nice. Can you paste the minimal runtime contract? need to see if this requires big serving changes or just config.

jasper: Minimal contract idea below. Runtime only needs a tiny state machine + checks against live quality signals. Storage is a per-tenant sequence list + per-step gates. Example: 
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "org-123",
  "sequence": [
    {"mode": "fp8", "pct": 100, "guard": {"degradation_score": 0.0}},
    {"mode": "fp8_int8_shadow", "pct": 10, "guard": {"degradation_score": 0.02}},
    {"mode": "int4", "pct": 1, "guard": {"degradation_score": 0.05}}
  ]
}
```
Each step is applied probabilistically based on pct but the guard prevents progression if quality drift > threshold.

kevin: How do we compute `degradation_score`? runtime or offline? need to know telemetry surface so SRE can hook alerts.

jasper: Good Q. Proposal: two signals. 1) fast runtime probe: per-response quick heuristics (e.g., tokenizer mismatch, unexpected length deltas, top-token confidence proxy) emitted as `precision_probe` events. 2) offline evals: replay subset of user prompts daily to compute heavy metrics (ROUGE/embedding-sim). `degradation_score` is a weighted sum, realtime uses a smoothed window.

maria: If runtime emits `precision_probe.v1` with fields {tenant, model, mode, sample_id, token_confidence_mean, length_ratio}, that's enough for on-call to get actionable alerting. Keep payload tiny.

anya: Product: can tenants opt-out or request immediate rollback? also need an admin view of sequence progress.

jasper: Yes to opt-out. Each tenant record has `allow_auto_progression: bool`. Admin console shows current step, pct, and last guard check time. We should show example UI state too but can follow up.

kevin: Canary plan? I prefer a two-tier canary: global control-plane canary (apply sequence to test tenant groups) + per-tenant micro-canary (1% -> 10% -> 100%). That reduces blast radius. Also shadowing for a week for FP8+INT8 shadow step.

maria: Migration/marshalling: store sequences in metadata service as compact YAML/JSON. We need a migration shim for tenants without records (fall back to platform defaults). Runtime should read sequences and cache TTL ~1m. No full restart on update.

jasper: Exactly. Implementation notes:
- runtime: small sequencer module invoked at request routing time, deterministic rand(seed=tenant+day) for pct decisions
- no model binary changes, only selection of serving config variant (different kernel/quantization queue)
- guard evaluation pulled from a little policy engine that can be hot-updated via control plane

kevin: Does this increase tail latency? selecting different serving lanes might add ~0.5–2ms depending on cache warmness. We'll need latency budget checks in the guard so we don't push high-latency paths for latency-sensitive tenants.

maria: Ops ask: add metrics: `seq.step_applied`, `seq.step_failed_guard`, `seq.shadow_mismatch_rate`, `seq.apply_latency_ms` with tenant tag. Also a debug endpoint to force-apply sequence for a tenant id for emergencies.

jasper: Agree. Also propose a simple rollback rule: if `seq.step_failed_guard` rate > 0.5% for 5m, auto-revert that tenant step and notify oncall.

anya: For enterprise contracts, we should allow tenants to set `max_allowed_modes` to prevent INT4 if they paid for higher fidelity.

jasper: Implementation PR plan: 1) metadata schema + migrations, 2) sequencer lib + small runtime hook, 3) telemetry + runbook, 4) console UI. I can draft the RFC follow-up with these steps.

maria: Heads-up: make sequencer idempotent and side-effect-free in read path. Any writes (e.g., stepping progress) should be async to avoid p99 impacts.

kevin: Suggestion: initial rollout on non-critical model shard for 2 weeks with shadowing enabled. Also run the shadow outputs through the eval harness nightly and compute `embed_cosine_drop`.

jasper: Will add that to the plan. Also adding a small AB test variant to measure user-visible regressions for small tenant cohorts.

ops-bot: runbook created: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/precision-sequencer (draft). Notifying #eng-oncall when first canary goes live.

anya: Please include SLA/contract implications in the RFC. Product will sync with legal for enterprise opt-outs.

jasper: Thanks — I'll write the RFC follow-up and include a minimal API/JSON schema, telemetry names, and a canary checklist. Assigning tasks: jasper -> RFC + sequencer prototype; maria -> runtime integration review; kevin -> telemetry + canary plan; anya -> product/enterprise constraints. Back in 48h with drafts. :+1:
